scope: United States food producer-price and food trade-margin divergence, March-July 2026
purpose: Populate the Producer Cost-Margin Transmission lane with direct BLS evidence that food producer-price movement and food wholesale/retail trade margins can diverge materially across months. This record does not infer product-level manufacturer profit or profiteering from trade-margin movement alone.
source_authority: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Producer Price Index

measurement_boundary.final_demand_foods: PPI final-demand food producer selling-price index
measurement_boundary.food_alcohol_wholesaling: PPI trade-service margin index for food and alcohol wholesaling
measurement_boundary.food_alcohol_retailing: PPI trade-service margin index for food and alcohol retailing
measurement_boundary.important_distinction: BLS trade PPIs measure changes in margins received by wholesalers and retailers, generally selling price less acquisition price. They are not equivalent to manufacturer accounting profit, net income, or company-wide operating margin.

bounded_findings: Food producer-price movement and food retail/wholesale trade-margin movement were not state-equivalent across March-July 2026.

The June-to-July 2026 transition is a clear divergence example: final-demand food producer prices fell 0.9 percent while food-and-alcohol wholesale margins rose 2.9 percent and retail margins rose 2.1 percent.
The July year-over-year state also diverged: final-demand foods were down 0.1 percent while food-and-alcohol retail trade margins were up 5.5 percent.

This establishes the need for a separately observed margin state in Physical Economics. It does not, by itself, establish excess profit, manufacturer margin expansion, consumer exploitation, or causal pass-through.
required_join_evidence: manufacturer/processor cost and profit evidence where available
retailer and wholesaler accounting ratios where available
consumer effective price per physical unit
